snippet.title: The Olmec: They Came Before the Maya | Mesoamerica's First People | History Documentary for Sleep
snippet.description:
Long before the Maya watched the stars and long before the Aztec raised their capital on a lake, the Olmec civilization rose in the swamps and rainforests of Mexico's Gulf coast. Often hailed as the "mother culture" of Mesoamerica, the Olmecs exerted their influence between 1200 and 400 BC, and nearly everything we associate with ancient Mesoamerica, from the pyramid to the ballgame to the feathered serpent gods, can be traced back to them. Encyclopedia Britannica
This long, calm documentary tells the complete story of the Olmec: who they were, the colossal stone heads they carved from boulders hauled across miles of jungle, the cities of San Lorenzo and La Venta, and the deep mystery of why they vanished. Their art, characterized by colossal stone heads and intricate jade carvings, influenced the artistic traditions of later cultures, and their understanding of astronomy, reflected in their calendrical systems, contributed to the Maya's renowned astronomical achievements. Encyclopedia BritannicaEncyclopedia Britannica
Yet for all their importance, they remain among the most mysterious peoples of the ancient world. There is no surviving direct account of the Olmec's religious beliefs, unlike the Mayan Popol Vuh, or the Aztecs with their many codices, and their culture lasted until roughly 400 BCE, at which time their center of La Venta lay abandoned. We do not know what they called themselves, and the very name "Olmec" was given to them thousands of years later. LAC GeoLAC Geo
Settle in, relax, and let the story carry you back three thousand years to the dawn of civilization in the Americas. Whether you are here for the history or simply to drift off to sleep, this is the forgotten first chapter beneath everything you thought you knew about ancient Mexico.

snippet.title: The Entire History of Colombia Full Detailed 3 hours long Documentary
snippet.description:
Explore the entire history of Colombia in this full educational documentary, tracing the nation’s journey from its earliest Indigenous civilizations to the landmark peace processes of the modern era. This documentary offers a clear and comprehensive narrative of Colombia’s transformation across centuries—covering ancient cultures like the Muisca and Tairona, the impact of Spanish conquest, and the formation and collapse of Gran Colombia.

Follow Colombia as it moves through major turning points: the rise of political parties, the Thousand Days’ War, the loss of Panama, the coffee boom, and the dramatic social conflicts of the twentieth century. Learn how the Banana Massacre, the rise of Jorge Eliécer Gaitán, and the eruption of La Violencia shaped national identity and political struggle.

We also explore the emergence of guerrilla movements, the influence of drug cartels, the government’s response, and the complex path toward peace. This documentary is designed for viewers seeking accurate, engaging, and accessible historical storytelling with strong narrative flow and clear explanations.
Whether you’re a student, history enthusiast, or curious learner, this video will deepen your understanding of Colombia’s past and its ongoing search for peace.

snippet.title: The LOST Chapters of Earth | Why Do So Many History Gaps Still Have No Explanation?
snippet.description:
Why do the most important transitions in Earth’s story simply vanish?
Why do civilizations, species, climates, and entire epochs appear suddenly, while everything before them dissolves into silence?
In this calm, late-night documentary, we explore The Lost Chapters of Earth -the history gaps that science can measure but still cannot fully explain.
Across geology, archaeology, paleontology, linguistics, and paleoclimate research, a strange pattern emerges:

 Earth remembers its turning points… but forgets the centuries around them.
This documentary guides you softly through:

• Boundary layers marking abrupt global transitions
• Extinction events preserved as razor-thin lines
• Cities that appear fully formed without developmental stages
• Civilizations whose writing stops the moment their world fractures
• Manuscripts lost because their materials were too fragile
• Species entering the fossil record without ancestors
• Climate shifts too fast for sediments to capture
• Human migrations that leave almost no archaeological continuity
• Civilizations built from wood, reeds, and earth that the planet cannot keep
• Writing systems that died before anyone could teach them
• Myths that preserve memories archaeology cannot
• Modern scientific tools revealing even wider gaps than we expected
• And the final question: why were these chapters lost?

snippet.title: Pseudoscience: An Amusing History of Crackpot Ideas and Why We Love Them (Nate Pedersen)
snippet.description:
From the easily disproved to the wildly speculative, to straight-up hucksterism, "Pseudoscience" is a romp through much more than bad science—it’s a light-hearted look into why we insist on believing in things such as Bigfoot, astrology, and the existence of aliens. 

Nate Pedersen is an award-winning nonfiction writer and anthologist living in southern Minnesota.  In addition to Pseudoscience, he and Lydia Kang, MD have co-authored "Quackery: A Brief History of the Worst Ways to Cure Everything" and "Patient Zero: A Curious History of the World's Worst Diseases," all published by Workman / Hachette.

snippet.title: The ENTIRE Story of the Danish Empire Detailed Documentary
snippet.description:
Sail through more than a millennium as this documentary traces how a seafaring people built, lost, and reinvented an empire. We begin with market towns and longships, then follow the rise of Christian kingship, the bold North Sea realm of Sweyn Forkbeard and Cnut, and the Baltic turn under the Valdemars and Absalon. Watch Margaret the First forge a union across three crowns, then see Sweden’s break reshape the map. 

The Lutheran Reformation binds Norway to Copenhagen and funds a stronger state; Christian the Fourth bets on shipyards, commerce, and early colonies from India to the Caribbean. Learn about the historical origins and development of the history of the Antichrist in this comprehensive documentary. Explore the connections between the book of Revelation, the number 666, and the ancient ruins of the Dead Sea.

The number 666 remains the most famous code in human history. Most people associate the number with the Bible or dark movie scripts, yet very few understand the actual historical context of these ancient symbols. This documentary investigates the specific moments when these ideas first appeared in writing and how they changed the course of Western thought.

Travel through the caves of Qumran where the earliest apocalyptic ideas were born. See how the fires of ancient Rome and the actions of Emperors like Nero provided the raw material for the book of Revelation. Witness the power struggles of the Middle Ages where the accusation of being a dark figure became the ultimate political tool for emperors and popes alike.

This journey reveals how a handful of cryptic verses from the ancient world became a universal blueprint for identifying ultimate evil. By understanding the history of this idea, we gain insight into human psychology and our persistent need to find meaning in times of crisis. This story explains how an idea can become more powerful than any flesh and blood individual.

snippet.title: 6. Easter Island - Where Giants Walked
snippet.description:
SUPPORT THE SHOW AND WATCH AD-FREE: http://patreon.com/fallofcivilizations_podcast

On one of the world’s most isolated islands, hundreds of vast stone statues lie mouldering in the grass. 

In this episode, we take a look at one of archaeology’s most enduring puzzles: the mystery of Easter Island. Find out how this unique community grew up in complete isolation, severed from the rest of the world by a vast expanse of ocean. Discover the incredible story of how it survived for so many centuries, and examine the evidence about what happened to finally bring this society, and its statues, crashing down.

This episode, we're joined by children from the Toki School of Music and Arts on Rapa Nui, who were kind enough to record some traditional ancestral chants especially for the podcast. 

Since 2012, Toki has offered children & adolescents free classes in classical and traditional music, with the aim of keeping the traditions of the island alive.

It's an incredible project, and if you want to help keep it running, you can donate here: https://tokirapanui.org/en/

snippet.title: No Blueprint for the Moon: Navigating the Unknowns of Extraterrestrial Construction (Caitlin Ahrens)
snippet.description:
This presentation will examine lunar architecture not as science fiction, but as an applied problem in risk management, engineering under uncertainty, and evidence-based design. We will explore what it would actually mean to plan and build structures on the Moon, where our geotechnical data are sparse, environmental hazards are extreme, and many Earth-based design assumptions simply do not hold. We will delve into strategies for site planning in an extreme, unfamiliar environment, where Earth-based assumptions must be rethought. Key challenges discussed include working with limited data, potential hazards from the environment, and the need for adaptable, resilient design solutions in lunar conditions.

Dr. Caitlin Ahrens is an assistant research scientist at NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, and the University of Maryland. She is a member of the Diviner Science Team with the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter. In collaboration with Artemis, she serves as a technical support scientist to assist in risk assessments of astronaut, rover, and lander activity at the lunar surface. Dr. Ahrens is Principal Investigator on a recent lunar sustainability work funded by the (former) NASA Office of Technology, Policy and Strategy. She also is a member of the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) working on how lunar architectures should be monitored for hazards, including construction, at the lunar surface.

snippet.title: From the Black Death to COVID: How Pandemics Remade the World
snippet.description:
From the Plague of Justinian to the Black Death, from smallpox in the Americas to the pandemic you lived through yourself, six catastrophes across two thousand years did more to shape the world you live in than any king, any war, or any revolution ever taught in a classroom.
This is not a story about how plagues destroyed the world. It is a story about how they built it. Across two thousand years, the same pattern repeats: a pandemic empties a society, and in that emptiness, the survivors inherit unprecedented leverage, the authorities who promised safety are exposed, and the question of who to believe is thrown wide open. The weekend, the modern wage, the end of serfdom, the Renaissance, the birth of public health, the way you worked through the most recent pandemic — trace them back far enough, and you find a disease, not a hero.
Join us as we trace this hidden pattern from the Plague of Justinian in the sixth century, through the Black Death that killed a third of Europe, the smallpox pandemics that erased the great civilizations of the Americas, the cholera outbreaks that gave birth to modern public health, the influenza of nineteen eighteen that the world chose to forget, and finally to the pandemic in living memory — and discover why history was written by the plagues.

snippet.title: Reconquista of Spain: How the Moors Were Defeated and an Empire Was Born
snippet.description:
For seven hundred and eighty-one years, three faiths shared one peninsula. Muslims, Christians, and Jews built the most sophisticated civilisation in medieval Europe, in the same cities, the same courts, and the same libraries. Then one side decided the coexistence was a problem to be solved. What followed was not simply a war. It was the founding event of the modern world.
This is the full history of the Reconquista of Spain, from the Moorish crossing of Gibraltar in 711 to the fall of Granada in 1492 and beyond. The rise of Al-Andalus and the golden age of Cordoba. The centuries of shifting alliances, Muslim rulers hiring Christian knights, Christian kings paying tribute to Moorish emirs. El Cid fighting for both sides. The slow hardening of the religious war narrative and the political machinery that built it. The single year, 1492, in which the fall of Granada, the expulsion of the Jews, and the commission of Columbus happened within months of each other, driven by the same logic. And the Spanish Empire that carried that logic across the ocean and applied it to an entirely new hemisphere.
This is not the version you were taught. It is the complete one.

snippet.title: Rick Prelinger | Lost Landscapes 02025: YEAR 20!
snippet.description:
LOST LANDSCAPES OF SAN FRANCISCO doubly celebrates this year! First, our 20th anniversary, and second, San Francisco itself — center of creativity, style, resistance and freedom. The city shines throughout this wide-ranging, unbounded panorama made from 128 years of San Francisco moving images with a soundtrack made by the audience as the film plays. 

Drawn from some 300 newly-unearthed archival films, LOST LANDSCAPES 20 recreates the textures and activities of everyday life, labor and play, replaying known and unknown historical moments, daylighting lost and found infrastructures, revealing the scars of settlement and pointing to more hopeful futures. Highlights include transportation in the air, water and on the land; images of the City's rich and resilient communities; unfamiliar footage of familiar places; countercultures and counterdemonstrators; and unpredictable moments on the streets.

Each year, LOST LANDSCAPES Patron Tickets support about 25% of Prelinger Library's annual budget. Please consider supporting this famed South of Market experimental research library, going strong after 20 years, that provides access to artists, historians, community members, researchers and readers of all kinds!

This talk was presented December 3, 02025 at the Herbst Theater in San Francisco. 
    
This talk is part of Long Now Talks.

Launched by Stewart Brand in 02003, Long Now Talks has invited more than 400 leading thinkers to share their civilization-scale ideas with a live audience and millions around the globe tuning in to our podcast and videos. Long Now Talks are brought to you by The Long Now Foundation, which has spent the last 25 years igniting cultural imagination around long-term thinking.

By inspiring thought and conversation about how we've been shaped by the last 10,000 years and what might be in store for us over the next 10,000 years, Long Now Talks seek to expand our collective sense of the present moment. Long Now Talks cover futurism and speculative fiction; time, nature, and contemplative practices; the intersection of the humanities and sciences; the evolution of counterculture to cyberculture; cultural imagination, land art and public monuments; and of course, long-term thinking and being a good ancestor.

In our age of compounding crises, The Long Now Foundation is a counterweight. We are a force that imagines new possibilities, thinks critically, and takes action over the long term. We believe that when we all come together, bound by commitment and curiosity, audacious things become possible. Will you join us?  https://longnow.org/join

snippet.title: The Library of Alexandria: The Truth About What Was Actually Lost
snippet.description:
The Library of Alexandria is the most famous library in history. But almost everything you have been told about it is incomplete. It did not burn in a single fire. It was not destroyed by one villain with a torch. And what was lost was not primarily scrolls.
At its peak, the Library of Alexandria was the ancient world's only state-funded research institution. A live-in campus of scholars, paid by Egyptian kings to do nothing but think. Inside its walls, Eratosthenes calculated the circumference of the Earth with two sticks. Aristarchus proposed that the Earth orbits the Sun, seventeen centuries before Copernicus. Hero of Alexandria built a working steam engine. Herophilus mapped the human brain. Euclid wrote the geometry textbook that would remain in use for over two thousand years.
This is the full story of the great Library of Alexandria. How it was built, who built it and why, what it produced, and how it was slowly, quietly, and entirely preventably allowed to die. The truth about what was actually lost is not a story about fire. It is a story about a system. And it is more unsettling than any fire could be.

snippet.title: The Great Recession: How 2008 Happened, and Who Paid for It
snippet.description:
The Great Recession was not just a crash on Wall Street. It was the moment the safest thing an ordinary person owned, their home, was quietly turned into a gamble by people they would never meet. This is the full story of the great recession and the global financial crisis of two thousand and eight, told clearly and without jargon, from the housing boom to the long and uneven recovery, for anyone who lived through it and was never quite shown how it really worked.

In this long form documentary we begin with the simplest question of all, what is a recession, and how it differs from a depression. We look back at nineteen twenty-nine and the walls that were built to make sure it could never happen again. Then we walk, step by patient step, through the machine behind the great recession, how millions of ordinary home loans were bundled, sliced, and sold around the world, how the whole structure rested on the belief that house prices could only rise, and what happened when that belief turned out to be false.

We follow the fall of two thousand and eight as it happened, the great banks brought to their knees, the bankruptcy that shook the world, and the weeks when the entire financial system came within days of collapse. And we follow it where it mattered most, into the lives of ordinary people, the families who lost homes they had bought responsibly, the workers whose jobs vanished, and the savers who watched a lifetime of careful work disappear. This is the human story of the great recession, of how the careful and the responsible were made to pay for a gamble they never knew was being placed in their name.

This is the story of what the great recession actually was, what caused it, who paid for it, and the harder question it leaves behind, of whether we ever truly learn to see these things coming, or only to give them new names. If you have ever wondered what really caused the two thousand and eight financial crisis, or how the great recession reached from Wall Street into ordinary homes, this is the complete account.

Settle in, and let us walk through the whole of it, from the height of the housing boom to the long shadow it left behind.
